mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC declines in every one of the four observed weeks (-8.6, -8.7, -8.9, -9.3), so the series carries persistent negative week-on-week momentum with no sign of inflection; that momentum carries into the next four weeks and the next 28-day mean falls below the trailing 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC falls monotonically from -8.6 at t-3w to -9.3 at t-0w
regime_hint: steady state with no new policy shock
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is greater than or equal to -8.9, the trailing 28-day mean, despite the four consecutive weekly declines.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES collapses 10.7 points in one week, from -5.6 to -16.3, crossing the threshold that marks a forced return to remote work; the resulting loss of weekday commuting removes the lunchtime and after-work discretionary trips that dominate retail-and-recreation footfall, so RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks is lower than over the last four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 8 points in a single week (observed: -5.6 to -16.3)
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES drops 10.7 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: Following any week in which WORKPLACES drops more than 8 points, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not lower than the trailing 28-day mean in the majority of cases.

mechanism_narrative: The joint signal of WORKPLACES falling 10.7 points and RESIDENTIAL rising 1.8 points to 11.1 in the same week identifies household time being reallocated from offices to homes; because this substitution is immediate rather than gradual, retail-and-recreation trips drop within one week and the next 28-day mean is lower than the trailing mean.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week change below -8 points occurring together with a RESIDENTIAL week-on-week gain above 1 point
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL reaches its four-week high of 11.1 in the same week WORKPLACES reaches its four-week low of -16.3
failure_condition: When WORKPLACES drops more than 8 points and RESIDENTIAL rises more than 1 point in the same week, RETAIL_REC in the following week is flat or higher.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS rebounds 7.2 points from -12.9 to -5.7, breaking a two-week weather-suppressed pattern; the same seasonal improvement in outdoor conditions raises willingness to leave home for non-essential errands, so retail-and-recreation mobility follows PARKS upward and the next 28-day mean exceeds the trailing mean.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 5 points week-on-week (observed: -12.9 to -5.7)
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumps 7.2 points from t-1w to t-0w after two weeks of decline
regime_hint: seasonal transition to milder outdoor conditions
failure_condition: In weeks where PARKS rises more than 5 points, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is equal to or below its trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM is the only series trending toward baseline, improving from -4.1 to -1.1 across the window; restored routine essential errands rebuild trip-chaining habits, and those chains carry households into adjacent retail-and-recreation destinations, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improves 3.0 points from -4.1 at t-3w to -1.1 at t-0w
regime_hint: steady state with gradual normalization of essential errands
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than or equal to -8.9, its trailing mean, even though GROCERY_PHARM closed the window within 2 points of baseline.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT falls 2.5 points week-on-week to -15.6, near its four-week low, showing that transit-accessed commercial corridors are losing trips; retail-and-recreation establishments in those corridors depend on transit-borne footfall, so RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks is dragged further below its trailing level.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls at least 2 points week-on-week (observed: -13.1 to -15.6)
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT drops 2.5 points from t-1w to t-0w and ends at -15.6
regime_hint: steady state with suppressed transit ridership
failure_condition: After weeks in which TRANSIT falls at least 2 points, RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean is not lower than its trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL reaching its four-week high of 11.1 while WORKPLACES hits its four-week low of -16.3 is the signature of a formal capacity restriction on gatherings; while that restriction regime remains in force, retail-and-recreation venues operate below capacity and RETAIL_REC stays lower over the next four weeks than over the last four.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 11.0 while WORKPLACES falls below -16.0
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 11.1 and WORKPLACES at -16.3 jointly mark the window extreme at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL exceeds 11.0 and WORKPLACES falls below -16.0 but RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean is at or above its trailing 28-day mean, the restriction-tightening mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS rising 7.2 points while TRANSIT falls 2.5 points in the same week identifies substitution from transit-accessed commercial districts toward nearby outdoor space; this substitution removes shopping-linked trips from retail-and-recreation venues, so RETAIL_REC is lower within one week of the divergence.
candidate_trigger: PARKS gains more than 5 points week-on-week while TRANSIT loses more than 2 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS gains 7.2 points and TRANSIT loses 2.5 points between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: When PARKS gains more than 5 points and TRANSIT loses more than 2 points in the same week, RETAIL_REC in the following week is flat or higher.
